_notes: Kaynak: docs/research/08-egzersiz-havuzu-taslagi.md — Hareket havuzu (72 hareket), tablo sırası korunmuştur (#1-72, 7 bölge x 10-12 hareket).
Mekanik çeviri: tüm kullanıcıya görünen alanlar (nameEn, dose.raw, regression, progression, safetyNote, cameraNote) Türkçe kaynaktan İngilizceye çevrilmiştir.

Wellness dil kısıtı: kaynaktaki tanı adları (Aşil tendinopati, disk hernisi, siyatik, osteoporoz, kalça impingement, rotator manşet, servikal radikülopati, vertigo, labrum yaralanması vb.) safetyNote alanlarında NÖTRLEŞTİRİLDİ — semptom/his diliyle yeniden yazıldı, tanı adı verilmedi.
Tip kısaltmaları (kaynak): dyn->dynamic, static->static_hold, circle->joint_circle, loaded->loaded_stretch, breath->breathing.
dose.reps alanı hold-bazlı hareketlerde set sayısını, döngü-bazlı hareketlerde döngü sayısını temsil eder (şema yalnız reps+holdSeconds sunuyor, ayrı 'sets' alanı yok).
Ekipman gerektiren varyantlar (ör. direnç bandı) progression alanına yazılmadı; kaynakta ekipmansız alternatif verilmeyen durumlarda null bırakıldı (#7, #40).
expertReviewRequired=true yalnız kaynağın '"Uzman doğrulaması şart" işaretli riskli hareketler' listesindeki 7 hareket için işaretlendi (#27, #31, #37, #42, #43, #47, #61).

exercises.nameEn: Standing ankle circles
exercises.regression: Perform seated
exercises.progression: Balance on one leg
exercises.safetyNote: Stop if the ankle feels painful

exercises.nameEn: Seated ankle pumps (dorsiflexion/plantarflexion)
exercises.regression: Start with a small range of motion
exercises.progression: Slow tempo with a pause at end range (no band needed)
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe

exercises.nameEn: Wall ankle dorsiflexion rock (knee-to-wall)
exercises.regression: Stand farther from the wall
exercises.progression: Move closer to the wall for a deeper lunge
exercises.safetyNote: Stop if you feel sharp pain at the back of your ankle

exercises.nameEn: Standing calf static stretch (wall lean)
exercises.regression: Bend the knee (targets the soleus)
exercises.progression: Straighten the knee and lean weight forward
exercises.safetyNote: Skip if you have sudden sharp pain or swelling in the back of your lower leg

exercises.nameEn: Downward-dog calf pedaling
exercises.regression: Keep a slight bend in the knees
exercises.progression: Press the heel down toward the floor
exercises.safetyNote: Modify if you have wrist discomfort

exercises.nameEn: Toe yoga (lifting the big toe and other toes separately)
exercises.regression: Use your hand to help lift the toes
exercises.progression: Do it while standing on one leg
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe
exercises.cameraNote: small toe movement depends on camera resolution

exercises.nameEn: Ankle inversion/eversion controlled circles
exercises.regression: Use a small range of motion
exercises.safetyNote: Progress slowly if your ankle tends to feel unstable

exercises.nameEn: Seated shin stretch (kneeling-free variant, top-of-foot stretch)
exercises.regression: Use your hand for light support
exercises.progression: Shift your weight to deepen the stretch
exercises.safetyNote: Modify if you feel knee discomfort

exercises.nameEn: Standing heel raises (controlled tempo)
exercises.regression: Hold onto a wall for support
exercises.progression: Perform on one leg
exercises.safetyNote: Use support if you have balance difficulties

exercises.nameEn: Ankle alphabet (tracing letters in the air with your foot)
exercises.regression: Use a shortened movement
exercises.progression: Trace the full alphabet with a larger range of motion
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe

exercises.nameEn: 90/90 hip switch
exercises.regression: Use your hands for support and move slowly
exercises.progression: Lift hands off the floor for a controlled, hands-free transition
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range smaller if your hip feels pinched

exercises.nameEn: Standing controlled hip circles (controlled alternative to leg swings)
exercises.regression: Use a small range of motion, hand on a wall for support
exercises.progression: Larger range of motion, without support
exercises.safetyNote: Use a wall for support if you have balance difficulties

exercises.nameEn: Kneeling hip flexor static stretch (half-kneeling lunge)
exercises.regression: Use a short-step standing lunge instead
exercises.progression: Elevate the back foot
exercises.safetyNote: Use a pillow or folded blanket under the knee if it feels uncomfortable

exercises.nameEn: Standing forward fold (hamstring and posterior chain)
exercises.regression: Bend the knees
exercises.progression: Straighten the knees and reach toward the floor
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your lower back feels sensitive

exercises.nameEn: Figure-4 seated/lying glute stretch
exercises.regression: Sit in a chair
exercises.progression: Lie on your back and pull the knee toward your chest
exercises.safetyNote: Move into this position carefully if you have specific hip movement precautions from a clinician

exercises.nameEn: Deep squat hold (generic name for ATG squat / malasana-like pose)
exercises.regression: Use hand support or an elevated heel
exercises.progression: No hand support, heels flat on the floor
exercises.safetyNote: Limit the depth if your hip or knee feels sensitive or you have movement precautions from a clinician

exercises.nameEn: Standing lateral leg swing (controlled)
exercises.regression: Hold a wall and use a small range of motion
exercises.progression: Free-standing, larger range of motion
exercises.safetyNote: Use support if balance is a concern

exercises.nameEn: Seated butterfly stretch
exercises.regression: Sit with back support
exercises.progression: Lean forward to deepen the stretch
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you feel hip or groin discomfort

exercises.nameEn: Rotational lunge stretch (generic name for the 'world's greatest stretch')
exercises.regression: Remove the rotation, do the lunge only
exercises.progression: Add the rotation plus an arm reach
exercises.safetyNote: Reduce the range if balance or spinal rotation feels limited

exercises.nameEn: Standing hip hinge (Romanian deadlift pattern, no equipment)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion with bent knees
exercises.progression: Single-leg hip hinge
exercises.safetyNote: Move carefully and keep a neutral spine if your lower back feels sensitive

exercises.nameEn: Supine piriformis stretch (crossed-leg pull)
exercises.regression: Keep feet on the floor with a gentle pull
exercises.progression: Pull the knee fully toward your chest
exercises.safetyNote: Keep this gentle if you feel pain or tingling radiating down your leg

exercises.nameEn: Standing quad stretch (includes a kneeling alternative)
exercises.regression: Perform lying on your side
exercises.progression: Hold your ankle with your hand and press it forward
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your knee feels sensitive or you've had a knee procedure

exercises.nameEn: Quadruped thoracic rotation (generic name for 'open book': thoracic rotation reach)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller rotation
exercises.progression: Full rotation while following your hand with your eyes
exercises.safetyNote: Switch to your forearms if you feel wrist discomfort

exercises.nameEn: Cat-cow (segmental spinal flexion/extension)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Sync with your breath, full range of motion
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your back feels sensitive

exercises.nameEn: Seated thoracic rotation
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Cross arms over chest, full rotation
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe

exercises.nameEn: Thread the needle
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Bring the shoulder fully to the floor
exercises.safetyNote: Be careful if you feel pinching in your neck or shoulder

exercises.nameEn: Standing extension over chair back (generic name: standing thoracic extension)
exercises.regression: Use a small extension
exercises.progression: Full extension with arms overhead
exercises.safetyNote: Check with a clinician before doing this if your bones or spine feel fragile, and keep the range small

exercises.nameEn: Wall slides (thoracic and shoulder combination)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Keep full contact with the wall, arms all the way up
exercises.safetyNote: Reduce the range if your shoulder feels pinched

exercises.nameEn: Side-lying windmill (open-chain thoracic rotation)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller rotation
exercises.progression: Full rotation, following the top hand with your eyes
exercises.safetyNote: Be careful if your shoulder tends to feel unstable

exercises.nameEn: Standing side bend (lateral thoracic and lumbar)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Reach your arm overhead to deepen the stretch
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your lower back feels sensitive

exercises.nameEn: Prone press-up (generic name for cobra-like pose: prone spinal extension)
exercises.regression: Stay on your forearms (smaller range of motion)
exercises.progression: Fully extend your arms
exercises.safetyNote: Stop if pain stays centered in your back; check with a clinician first if you feel pain radiating down your leg

exercises.nameEn: Segmental cat-cow with breath pacing
exercises.regression: Do the movement only, without breath pacing
exercises.progression: Deepen with a longer exhale
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe
exercises.cameraNote: the breathing component cannot be measured by camera

exercises.nameEn: Shoulder circles (arm circles)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Larger range of motion, arms fully extended
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your shoulder tends to feel unstable

exercises.nameEn: Cross-body shoulder stretch
exercises.regression: Use a gentle pull
exercises.progression: Use your other hand to pull deeper
exercises.safetyNote: Be careful if you have a shoulder injury

exercises.nameEn: Overhead triceps/lat stretch
exercises.regression: Bend the elbow only slightly
exercises.progression: Bend the elbow fully and pull with the other hand
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you feel pinching in your neck or shoulder

exercises.nameEn: Wall pec stretch (doorway-free variant)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller angle
exercises.progression: Arm above 90 degrees, rotate the torso
exercises.safetyNote: Be careful if the front of your shoulder tends to feel unstable

exercises.nameEn: Behind-the-back shoulder extension reach (generic name: shoulder internal rotation reach)
exercises.regression: Use a towel or piece of clothing for assistance, or try reaching your hand toward your shoulder blade without one
exercises.progression: Clasp your hands together behind your back
exercises.safetyNote: Stop without forcing if your shoulder feels weak or painful
exercises.cameraNote: visibility depends on camera angle behind the back

exercises.nameEn: Scapular retraction/protraction (controlled)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Full retraction with an isometric hold
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe
exercises.cameraNote: shoulder blade movement is not always clearly visible on camera, depends on clothing fit

exercises.nameEn: Wall angels
exercises.regression: Raise the arms only partway
exercises.progression: Full raise, with back and head touching the wall
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you feel pinching in your shoulder

exercises.nameEn: Standing shoulder external rotation (elbow at side, equipment-free isometric)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller angle
exercises.safetyNote: Start light if your shoulder feels weak
exercises.cameraNote: the isometric contraction itself cannot be verified by camera, only the position is visible

exercises.nameEn: Standing arm swings (front/back)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Use a larger range of motion
exercises.safetyNote: Be careful if your shoulder tends to feel unstable

exercises.nameEn: Neck-shoulder combined roll
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Full range of motion, slow tempo
exercises.safetyNote: Check with a clinician first if you have sudden or acute neck pain

exercises.nameEn: Neck flexion/extension (chin-to-chest / gentle look-up)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Full range of motion, slow tempo
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your neck feels sensitive or you have a history of neck injury

exercises.nameEn: Neck lateral flexion (ear-to-shoulder)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller angle
exercises.progression: Add gentle hand pressure
exercises.safetyNote: If you feel tingling or pain radiating into your arm, be careful and skip adding hand pressure

exercises.nameEn: Neck rotation (look left/right)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Full range of motion
exercises.safetyNote: Progress slowly if you have a history of dizziness

exercises.nameEn: Chin tucks (cervical retraction)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller retraction
exercises.progression: Hold the isometric position longer
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe, and helpful for a neutral neck posture
exercises.cameraNote: small movement, sensitive to camera angle

exercises.nameEn: Neck circles, gentle half-circle only (full 360-degree circles are not offered)

dose.raw: 4-5 reps per direction, half-circle only (front-to-side, no full backward extension)

exercises.regression: Use only the flexion/lateral half-circle
exercises.safetyNote: Full cervical extension combined with rotation carries a safety risk — no progression beyond the half-circle is offered

exercises.nameEn: Isometric neck press (4 directions, hand resistance)
exercises.regression: Use light pressure
exercises.progression: Increase the pressure
exercises.safetyNote: Start at low intensity if you have acute neck pain
exercises.cameraNote: isometric hand-to-head contact and force cannot be measured by camera

exercises.nameEn: Upper trapezius stretch (head tilt with a gentle pull)
exercises.regression: No hands, head tilt only
exercises.progression: Add a gentle hand pull
exercises.safetyNote: Skip adding hand pressure if you feel tingling or pain radiating into your arm

exercises.nameEn: Levator scapulae stretch (look down and across)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller angle
exercises.progression: Add gentle hand support
exercises.safetyNote: Start gently if you have neck pain

exercises.nameEn: Seated posture reset (breathing, spinal lengthening plus chin tuck)
exercises.regression: Use a shorter duration
exercises.progression: Hold for longer
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe
exercises.cameraNote: the breathing component cannot be measured, but posture is visible

exercises.nameEn: Standing gentle neck side-glide
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Full range of motion
exercises.safetyNote: Slow down if you have a history of dizziness

exercises.nameEn: Standing side bend (lateral flexion, full body)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Reach your arm overhead to deepen
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you have acute lower back pain

exercises.nameEn: Standing side lunge (lateral lunge, no equipment)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion, shallow lunge
exercises.progression: Deeper lunge, push the hips back
exercises.safetyNote: Limit the depth if you have knee or hip pain

exercises.nameEn: Seated IT band/lateral hip stretch (crossed-leg twist)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller rotation
exercises.progression: Full rotation, using your arm for support
exercises.safetyNote: Be careful if your lower back rotation feels limited

exercises.nameEn: Standing lateral reach with breath
exercises.regression: Use a smaller reach
exercises.progression: Reach fully
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe

exercises.nameEn: Side plank hold (short duration, lateral chain control)
exercises.regression: On the knee (modified)
exercises.progression: On the foot, full body
exercises.safetyNote: Modify if you have shoulder or wrist pain

exercises.nameEn: Lateral neck-to-hip continuous side stretch (full-body lateral chain)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Arm fully overhead, full side bend
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you have acute back or shoulder pain

exercises.nameEn: Standing lateral leg swing (in/out, hip abductor/adductor)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion with support
exercises.progression: Larger range of motion, without support
exercises.safetyNote: Use support if balance is a concern

exercises.nameEn: Seated adductor (groin) stretch (butterfly variant with forward lean)
exercises.regression: Use back support
exercises.progression: Lean forward to deepen
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you have groin or hip pain

exercises.nameEn: Standing quadratus lumborum release (side bend plus rotation combination)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Full range of motion plus breath
exercises.safetyNote: Check with a clinician first if you have ongoing lower back pain

exercises.nameEn: Wide-stance side-to-side rock (lateral hip mobility)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion, shallow rock
exercises.progression: Deeper rock, shift your weight fully
exercises.safetyNote: Limit the depth if you have knee or hip pain

exercises.nameEn: Standing hamstring stretch (forward fold variant, single leg)
exercises.regression: Bend the knee
exercises.progression: Straighten the knee, fold fully forward
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your lower back feels sensitive

exercises.nameEn: Seated single-leg hamstring stretch
exercises.regression: Keep the knee bent for support
exercises.progression: Straighten the knee, reach forward
exercises.safetyNote: Generally safe

exercises.nameEn: Standing calf-to-hamstring chain stretch (generic name: inverted-V stretch, downward-dog-like)
exercises.regression: Bend the knees
exercises.progression: Straighten the knees, heels close to the floor
exercises.safetyNote: Change your hand position if you feel wrist discomfort

exercises.nameEn: Good morning pattern (bodyweight hip hinge, posterior chain activation)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Full range of motion, slow tempo
exercises.safetyNote: Move carefully and keep a neutral spine if you have acute lower back pain

exercises.nameEn: Bird-dog (posterior chain control plus core)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion (arm or leg only, one at a time)
exercises.progression: Move the opposite arm and leg together, add a hold
exercises.safetyNote: Stay in a smaller range of motion if balance is a concern

exercises.nameEn: Glute bridge (posterior chain activation plus gentle stretch)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Single-leg bridge, add a hold
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you have lower back pain

exercises.nameEn: Prone hamstring curl (controlled, equipment-free isometric variant)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion
exercises.progression: Slow tempo, add a hold
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if you have knee pain

exercises.nameEn: Standing forward fold with shoulder reach (posterior chain plus shoulder combination)
exercises.regression: Bend the knees
exercises.progression: Straighten the knees, hands to the floor
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your lower back feels sensitive

exercises.nameEn: Sphinx-to-child's pose flow (posterior chain relaxation flow)
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range of motion transition
exercises.progression: Full range of motion, slow breath-paced transition
exercises.safetyNote: Widen your knees in child's pose if you feel knee discomfort

exercises.nameEn: Seated forward fold with breath (hamstring plus relaxation, breath-paced)
exercises.regression: Bend the knees
exercises.progression: Straighten the knees, long exhale
exercises.safetyNote: Keep the range small if your lower back feels sensitive
